title: Larb Moo
subtitle: Thai minced pork salad with toasted rice and herbs
excerpt: Larb moo is a minced pork salad from northern Thailand and Laos. The meat is cooked briefly, then tossed with fish sauce, lime juice, toasted rice powder, and fresh herbs. It is light, zingy, and very quick to make. Serve with steamed rice or lettuce leaves.
sourceNotes: Larb (also spelled laab or laap) is the national dish of Laos and a staple of northern Thai (Isaan) cuisine. The dish is served at celebrations and is considered food that brings good luck. The toasted rice powder (khao khua) is an essential texture element -- it adds a nutty crunch and helps absorb the dressing.

content.text: The toasted rice powder is what makes larb different from any other minced meat dish. It takes 5 minutes to make and cannot be skipped. Toast the rice dry, grind it rough, and stir it in at the end. The powder absorbs the dressing and adds a faint nuttiness that holds the whole dish together.

items.prepNote: use 2 tbsp toasted rice powder -- toast 2 tbsp uncooked rice in a dry pan until golden, then grind

content.text: Toast 2 tablespoons of raw rice in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until golden. Grind to a rough powder in a pestle and mortar or spice grinder. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat. Add the pork mince. Cook, breaking it up, for 4 to 5 minutes until just cooked through. Do not brown it -- it should stay pale and tender.
Remove from the heat. Add the fish sauce, lime juice, chilli flakes, and toasted rice powder. Toss together.
Add the shallots and spring onion. Toss again.
Taste and adjust -- it should be sour, salty, and spicy with a nutty texture from the rice powder.
Serve at room temperature with fresh coriander, steamed rice, or lettuce leaves.

items.fix: Cook the pork over high heat and stop as soon as the pink colour is gone. It should be tender. The residual heat and the dressing will continue to carry the flavour -- overcooking makes it grainy.

content.text: Larb is the national dish of Laos and is deeply embedded in Isaan (northeastern Thai) culture. It is eaten at festivals and family gatherings. The toasted rice powder is not optional -- it gives a texture and nutty note that defines the dish. Fresh mint and coriander are the classic herbs.
